name: MS-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Guest running with large financial advantage
No polls or expert ratings; minimal Democratic fundraising
Markets price Republican win near certain
model.rationale: Guest is a renominated incumbent in a district that leans Republican by fourteen points, and he has raised far more money than his Democratic challenger. Prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 98%, and with no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing the challenger competitive, or major outside spending against Guest, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 3rd District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about fourteen points toward the GOP. Michael Guest, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and holds a large financial edge, having raised over $800,000 with nearly $1 million on hand. His Democratic challenger, Michael Chiaradio, has raised only about $155,000 and has minimal cash available, with no outside spending reported on either side. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 98%. The forecast points to a comfortable Guest win, with the main uncertainty being turnout patterns in a low-profile downballot race.
